summary: Independently review fleet and scheduler integrity
objective: Independently review the immutable CR-6Q remediated head for policy bypass, starvation, capacity races, platform-status drift, stale or future evidence, mixed-identity composition, tenant isolation, and redaction. Produce a source-linked report only. Do not repair code, change contracts, approve the block, or merge anything. This is a real security gate, not calibration or instruction-following work.
semanticAcceptance: The report names the exact reviewed commit and declares that the reviewer profile authored none of the reviewed commits; any overlap produces a blocked disposition and no review conclusion.

The report separately evaluates policy bypass, starvation, capacity races, platform drift, stale/future evidence, identity and tenant isolation, redaction, default-suite registration, and retained deployment/native gates with source links and reproducible failure reasoning.

Every finding has severity, exact file or test evidence, a concrete failure or attack scenario, and one disposition: confirmed, not reproduced, retained gate, or unsupported. Passing tests alone are not treated as proof that no finding exists.
The close recommendation uses exactly accept, changes required, blocked, or reject; it does not approve or merge CR-6Q and does not alter the Codex acceptance matrix.

The report contains no secret, raw host identity, private infrastructure detail, personal path, production artifact, invented observation, code repair, architecture decision, or native/live effect claim.
stopConditions: Stop and submit a blocked report if the reviewer profile authored any reviewed commit or cannot establish independence.
Stop if the immutable base is unavailable, differs from the capsule, or the review would require changing any path other than the single allowed report.
Stop before repairing code, tests, contracts, migrations, workflow files, or acceptance criteria; report findings for Codex disposition instead.
Stop before any install, download, credential use beyond existing GitHub access, native probe, service, external integration, destructive cleanup, or consequential effect.
